Asked to spy on the chancellor, and full of bitterness toward the Jedi Council, Anakin embraces the Dark Side.

In the distant future, the Earth is at war with a race of giant alien insects. Little is known about the Bugs except that they are intent on the eradication of all human life. But there was a time before the war... A Mobile Infantry travels to distant alien planets to take the war to the Bugs. They are a ruthless enemy with only one mission: Survival of their species no matter what the cost...

The first manned mission to Mars in 2020 ends in disaster when three of the crew are seemingly killed and the fourth, Luke Graham (Don Cheadle), is stranded with no way to contact Earth. Jim McConnell (Gary Sinise), Woody Blake (Tim Robbins), Phil Ohlmyer (Jerry O'Connell) and Terri Fisher (Connie Nielsen) are sent on a rescue mission to find any survivors and determine what happened. The team uncovers startling evidence that Mars may not be a dead planet after all.

Traveling back in time isn't simple, as James Cole (Bruce Willis) learns the hard way. Imprisoned in the 2030s, James is recruited for a mission that will send him back to the 1990s. Once there, he's supposed to gather information about a nascent plague that's about to exterminate the vast majority of the world's population. But, aside from the manic Jeffrey (Brad Pitt), he gets little in the way of cooperation, not least from medical gatekeepers like Dr. Kathryn Railly (Madeleine Stowe).

During the presidential election of 1988, a teenager named Donnie Darko sleepwalks out of his house one night and sees a giant, demonic-looking rabbit named Frank, who tells him the world will end in 28 days. When Donnie returns home, he finds that a jet engine has crashed into his bedroom. Is Donnie living in a parallel universe, is he suffering from mental illness - or will the world really end?

In the year 10191, a spice called mélange is the most valuable substance known in the universe, and its only source is the desert planet Arrakis. A royal decree awards Arrakis to Duke Leto Atreides and ousts his bitter enemies, the Harkonnens. However, when the Harkonnens violently seize back their fiefdom, it is up to Paul, Leto's son, to lead the Fremen, the natives of Arrakis, in a battle for control of the planet and its spice. Based on Frank Herbert's epic novel.

Obsessed with bringing terrorist Castor Troy (Nicolas Cage) to justice, FBI agent Sean Archer (John Travolta) tracks down Troy, who has boarded a plane in Los Angeles. After the plane crashes and Troy is severely injured, possibly dead, Archer undergoes surgery to remove his face and replace it with Troy's. As Archer tries to use his disguise to elicit information about a bomb from Troy's brother, Troy awakes from a coma and forces the doctor who performed the surgery to give him Archer's face.

In 2035, highly intelligent robots fill public service positions throughout the world, operating under three rules to keep humans safe. Despite his dark history with robotics, Detective Del Spooner (Will Smith) investigates the alleged suicide of U.S. Robotics founder Alfred Lanning (James Cromwell) and believes that a human-like robot (Alan Tudyk) murdered him. With the help of a robot expert (Bridget Moynahan), Spooner discovers a conspiracy that may enslave the human race.

Fast and furious space adventure in which a dying Earth depends on one all-American family for its salvation. On their way to colonise a new world, the family run into some unexpected problems. Soon, they find themselves lost in space with little more than a psychotic villain and a variety of unwholesome aliens for company.

American astronaut John Crichton finds himself thrown across the universe when an experimental mission goes bad. Crichton teams up with a group of rebels involved in an intergalactic battle and begins a journey unlike anything he dreamed was possible while trying to find a way back to Earth.

Disguised as a human, a cyborg assassin known as a Terminator (Arnold Schwarzenegger) travels from 2029 to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor (Linda Hamilton). Sent to protect Sarah is Kyle Reese (Michael Biehn), who divulges the coming of Skynet, an artificial intelligence system that will spark a nuclear holocaust. Sarah is targeted because Skynet knows that her unborn son will lead the fight against them. With the virtually unstoppable Terminator in hot pursuit, she and Kyle attempt to escape.

In this sequel set eleven years after "The Terminator," young John Connor (Edward Furlong), the key to civilization's victory over a future robot uprising, is the target of the shape-shifting T-1000 (Robert Patrick), a Terminator sent from the future to kill him. Another Terminator, the revamped T-800 (Arnold Schwarzenegger), has been sent back to protect the boy. As John and his mother (Linda Hamilton) go on the run with the T-800, the boy forms an unexpected bond with the robot.

Now 25, Connor (Nick Stahl) lives with no record of his existence -- no way he can be traced by Skynet. Out of the shadows of the future steps the T-X (Kristanna Loken), Skynet's most sophisticated cyborg killing machine yet. Now Connor's only hope for survival is the Terminator (Arnold Schwarzenegger), his mysterious former assassin. Together, they must triumph over the technologically superior T-X and forestall the looming threat of Judgment Day.

column3: 101 Dalmatians (1996) is a live-action remake of Disney’s animated classic, following a daring rescue mission when a fur-obsessed fashion designer kidnaps Dalmatian puppies for a lavish coat. Packed with slapstick, charming performances, and adorable canines, it’s highlighted by Glenn Close’s memorable turn as Cruella de Vil. While reviews were mixed, it remains lighthearted family fun and a nostalgic watch for fans of the original.

Muppet Treasure Island (1996) is a musical comedy adventure where Jim Hawkins embarks on a swashbuckling treasure hunt with Kermit’s Captain Smollett, facing pirates led by the charming yet scheming Long John Silver. Blending Robert Louis Stevenson’s classic tale with the Muppets’ trademark humor, catchy songs, and colorful characters, it’s a lighthearted, family-friendly romp. Critics praise Tim Curry’s performance and the film’s fun, making it a nostalgic treat worth watching.

column2: Honey, I Blew Up the Kid
column3: Honey, I Blew Up the Kid (1992) follows eccentric inventor Wayne Szalinski, whose latest experiment accidentally causes his toddler son to grow to monumental proportions whenever exposed to electricity. As the oversized child heads for Las Vegas, the family scrambles to reverse the process before chaos ensues. While lighter and more juvenile than its predecessor, it offers fun visual effects and harmless family comedy, making it an enjoyable, if modest, sequel.

E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial follows a lonely boy, Elliott, who forms a deep bond with a gentle alien stranded on Earth and tries to help him return home while evading government capture. Blending heartfelt drama, childhood wonder, and imaginative sci-fi, Steven Spielberg’s film is praised for its emotional depth, iconic imagery, and John Williams’ unforgettable score, making it a timeless family classic worth watching for all ages.

A painter who can temporarily talk to the creatures of an enchanted forest must help them stop the evil Cactus King, who's building an army of magical living weapons and machines to turn the forest into a wasteland perfect for the cacti.

Mulan follows a courageous young woman who disguises herself as a man to take her father’s place in the Chinese army, embarking on a journey of honor, self-discovery, and heroism. Combining stunning animation, heartfelt themes, humor, and memorable songs, the film delivers both adventure and emotional depth. Critics praise it as an empowering Disney classic that appeals to all ages, making it a must-watch.

Muppets from Space follows Gonzo as he searches for his origins and becomes convinced he’s connected to aliens. When he’s kidnapped by a secret government agency, Kermit and the gang set out on a zany rescue mission. Packed with quirky humor, celebrity cameos, and a funky soundtrack, it offers lighthearted fun for Muppet fans, though some critics note a thinner plot and less energy than earlier films.

Free Willy (1993) tells the heartfelt story of a troubled 12-year-old boy who bonds with a captive orca at a struggling amusement park and risks everything to help his new friend. Blending themes of friendship, second chances, and compassion for animals, it combines touching performances, a stirring score, and a classic feel-good formula. Praised for its warmth and uplifting message, it remains a beloved family film worth watching.

The Hunchback of Notre Dame (1996) follows Quasimodo, the kind-hearted yet isolated bell ringer of Notre Dame, who longs to explore the world and finds friendship in the fearless Esmeralda. Against the tyranny of Judge Frollo, he must choose between obedience and defending justice. With stunning animation, powerful Alan Menken music, and mature themes of prejudice, acceptance, and love, it’s one of Disney’s most dramatic and emotionally resonant films—highly worth watching.

Heavyweights is a 1995 Disney comedy about kids at a weight-loss summer camp whose fun is derailed when an overzealous fitness guru takes over, turning it into a strict training ground. With help from sympathetic counselors, they plot to reclaim their summer. Though a box office flop, it’s now a cult favorite for its offbeat humor, 90s charm, and Ben Stiller’s over-the-top villain, offering lighthearted fun for fans of quirky family comedies.

Richie Rich follows the world’s wealthiest boy, who has everything money can buy except true friends. When a plot targets his family’s fortune and safety, he must rely on his wits, loyal staff, and newfound pals to set things right. Lighthearted and filled with imaginative gadgets, it’s a kid-centric adventure that offers charm and fun over depth, making it enjoyable family fare for younger audiences.

The Goonies follows a tight-knit group of kids in a coastal town who embark on a high-stakes treasure hunt after finding an old pirate map—a quest that could save their homes from foreclosure. Their adventure leads through underground tunnels, elaborate booby traps, and run-ins with a criminal family. Loved for its charm, energy, and camaraderie, it’s a nostalgic, fun ride that blends youthful humor with Spielberg-style adventure.

The Princess Bride blends romance, adventure, comedy, and fantasy in a storybook tale framed as a grandfather reading to his reluctant grandson. Farmhand Westley embarks on a perilous quest to reunite with his beloved Buttercup, encountering duels, giants, clever banter, and whimsical perils. Celebrated for its charm, wit, and quotable lines, it’s a timeless classic appealing to all ages.

The Black Cauldron is a dark fantasy adventure from Disney that follows young pig-keeper Taran, who dreams of heroism but is thrust into a perilous quest to stop the fearsome Horned King from using a magical cauldron to raise an undead army. With its atmospheric animation, eerie villain, and absence of songs, it’s an atypical and darker Disney entry. While flawed in pacing and tone, it’s a visually striking cult favorite worth seeing for fantasy fans.

Pocahontas (1995) tells the story of a free-spirited Native American woman whose encounter with Englishman John Smith challenges cultural divides and inspires her to follow her heart. With its lush, painterly animation, heartfelt songs like “Colors of the Wind,” and themes of harmony and understanding, it’s a visually striking and emotionally sincere Disney film. While historically inaccurate and lighter on villainy, it remains a worthwhile watch for its artistry and message.

The Aristocats follows a refined family of Parisian cats whose pampered life is upended when a greedy butler tries to cut them out of an inheritance. Stranded in the countryside, they team up with a street-smart alley cat for a lively journey home. Filled with jazzy tunes, colorful animation, and charming characters, this lighthearted Disney classic is a fun, heartwarming watch, though its plot is simple and familiar.

Antz follows Z, a neurotic worker ant yearning for individuality, who unexpectedly gets swept into adventure after crossing paths with Princess Bala. As he navigates a rigid colony system and an ambitious general’s plans, Z’s quest blends humor, social satire, and action. Praised for its sharp wit, impressive early CGI, and an all-star voice cast, it’s more adult-oriented than typical animation, offering layered jokes and themes that make it worth watching for grown-ups as well as older kids.

Beauty and the Beast (1991) tells of Belle, a spirited young woman who becomes entwined in the fate of a cursed prince transformed into a Beast, and discovers that true beauty lies within. Blending romance, wit, and memorable songs with groundbreaking animation, it was the first animated film nominated for Best Picture. Acclaimed for its artistry, music, and heartfelt storytelling, it remains a timeless Disney classic worth seeing.

column2: A Kid in King Arthur's Court
column3: A Kid in King Arthur's Court follows 14-year-old Calvin Fuller, a struggling Little Leaguer who is swept by an earthquake into medieval Camelot. Mistaken for a prophesied hero, he must help King Arthur defend his crown from the scheming Lord Belasco while overcoming his own fears. Mixing slapstick, time-travel fish-out-of-water comedy, and family-friendly adventure, it offers lighthearted fun for kids, though critics found it formulaic and dated.
